eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 1, Lesson 3
subtitle: "What is a typical value?" — answered with a single number, three ways.

steps.label: MODE
steps.sub: Most frequent — works for categories too

code:
s = pd.Series([12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 30, 400])
print("mean  :", round(s.mean(), 2))   # 61.89
print("median:", s.median())          # 20.0
print("mode  :", s.mode().tolist())   # [15]
caption: Eight of nine orders are $30 or less — the mean describes almost nobody.

eyebrow: The median is robust; the mean is not
code:
t = s.drop(8)      # drop the $400 order
print(t.mean())    # 19.625  -- collapsed from 61.89
print(t.median())  # 19.0    -- barely moved from 20.0
caption: A big gap between mean and median is a warning sign: skew or outliers — check a chart.

code:
from scipy import stats
stats.trim_mean(s, 0.2)          # ~20.71 -- cuts the 12 and the 400

np.average([80, 100], weights=[3, 1])   # 85.0
caption: Trimming discards extremes before averaging; weighting counts some values more than others.
